# Preferred sources

Users can mark sites as preferred sources. Those sites become more visible in Top Stories and are labelled in AI Mode and AI Overviews. Author's view: it rewards brands people actively choose. On Day 3 Google said it can add a preferred-source badge, or a 'highly cited' badge, to a text result.

Based on: `D1-C027`, `D1-C028`, `D3-C317`.

## Where it was discussed

- **Day 1** (2026-09-30, Crawling): [What's new in the world of Search](../../40-sessions/day1/D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md) (1 claim); plus 1 documentation, press or analysis note
- **Day 3** (2026-10-02, Serving: Ranking, Search Console, and Performance): [How Search results are born](../../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) (1 claim)

## Shown and said at the event

- **[Slide]** Sites that users mark as a preferred source are more visible in Top Stories and are labelled in AI Mode and AI Overviews.
  <br><sub>`D1-C027` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs · Extended by [D3-C317](../../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google can add elements to a text result, such as a 'highly cited' badge or a preferred-source badge.
  <br><sub>`D3-C317` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Help your readers find your site through preferred sources in Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/preferred-sources) · Extends [D1-C027](../../40-sessions/day1/D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md)</sub>

## Analysis

- **[Analysis]** Preferred sources, linked subscriptions and Search profiles all depend on users acting on a brand's behalf. They reward brands with a loyal audience and do little for anonymous lead-generation sites.
  <br><sub>`D1-C028` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 1, What's new in the world of Search</sub>
